name: Perceptual Cache Coherence
local_research_lens: Treat learned visual familiarity as a versioned non-authoritative cache over current Retina sensor evidence. Cache hits require semantic/perceptual version coherence; mismatch, drift, ambiguity or weak evidence invalidates/forces deeper perception.
shared_program_connection: FRANK v0.1 adaptive visual learning; ClayCode BASE must express versioned prototype/classifier state, trusted evidence tiers, open-set decisions, promotion/rollback, resource budgets and replay.

hypotheses.proposition: Binding visual-memory cache entries to a perceptual/context epoch can sharply reduce stale false-familiarity fast-path errors under appearance drift while preserving most compute savings.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched-budget replay on real FRANK/Retina traces shows no reduction in false-familiarity or causes unacceptable escalation/latency overhead.

hypotheses.proposition: UnifiedDB state epochs plus ClayGraph graph epochs can provide enough version identity to invalidate stale visual familiarity without turning graph activation into sensor truth.
hypotheses.falsifier: A concrete H1/H2 trace requires visual-version semantics not representable by current state/graph epoch model.

hypotheses.proposition: ClayCode can represent cache-line lifecycle states VALID, SUSPECT, INVALID and REVALIDATING using existing typed state/effect semantics without a language redesign.
hypotheses.falsifier: Executable ClayCode counterexample shows existing G9 semantics cannot express deterministic version checks, atomic promotion/rollback or replayable invalidation.

counterhypotheses.proposition: A calibrated open-set threshold alone may provide equivalent safety; explicit cache coherence/versioning may add complexity without measurable value.
Perceptual epochs may invalidate too broadly, causing excessive deep Retina calls and erasing the intended compute benefit.

experiment.epistemic_limit: Synthetic mechanism test only. Does not establish FRANK hardware/data performance.

external_research.source: Bhatnagar et al., ICML 2023, Improved Online Conformal Prediction via Strongly Adaptive Online Learning
external_research.relevance: Online uncertainty sets can adapt under distribution shift; supports adaptive revalidation/abstention research, not the cache-coherence analogy itself.

external_research.source: Galashov et al., CoLLAs 2023, Continually learning representations at scale
external_research.relevance: Large pretrained frozen representations can remain competitive in continual-learning benchmarks; supports frozen-backbone/lightweight adaptation prior.

cross_branch_implications.retina: Add perceptual/context version identity to familiarity cache entries; fast path must require version coherence in addition to confidence/open-set gates.
cross_branch_implications.unifieddb: Persist classifier/prototype version, perceptual epoch/context hash, invalidation reason and last trusted revalidation receipt.
cross_branch_implications.claygraph: Graph activation/salience may point to cached familiar entities but must never satisfy version-coherence or sensor-truth checks by itself.
cross_branch_implications.claycode: BASE proof corpus should include a versioned cache invalidation/revalidation program with rollback and deterministic replay before language changes are considered.
cross_branch_implications.harness: Add PCC-E2 matched-budget replay: static threshold vs epoch-coherent vs epoch+drift detector on false familiarity, escalation rate, latency and recovery.
cross_branch_implications.frank: Treat visual memory as a performance cache over perception, not as perceptual authority.

negative_results: The synthetic result does not justify a global visual epoch; overly broad invalidation remains a live failure mode.
The result does not establish that cache coherence beats a well-calibrated open-set threshold on real traces.
next_test: PCC-E2 real H1/Retina replay with per-entity/per-context version scopes and threshold-only baseline.
